lines.trans: Which one do you want to get chewed out for first—the broadcast accident or the ratings?
Start with whichever one you feel like, sir.
You passed the entrance exam into a broadcasting station and cannot tell North Gyeongsang Goryeong from South Gyeongsang?
Wait—does North Gyeongsang Goryeong not sound weird? South Gyeongsang Goryeong sounds natural!
Director, it actually is North Gyeongsang Goryeong—writing South Gyeongsang is what caused the accident.
Oh, it really is confusing—which means you should have paid all the more attention!
We already phoned the county office to apologize and agreed to air an apology caption next week.
That is not the real problem right now—Goryeong is our station president's hometown!
Oh my goodness!
Pinpoint exactly who is responsible so I have something to say when I report upstairs!

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Wait—was I getting scolded by you back then?
This expression comes from 'got scolded'.

meanings.note: Compound of 방송 (broadcast) and 사고 (accident), referring to any unintended disruption during a live show. RR: bangsongsago.

examples.trans: A major on-air accident happened during the live broadcast.
If you are not careful, it is an on-air accident.
That drama has high viewer ratings.
The ratings went up a lot.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그냥 집으로 가자고 했어야 했는데 나도 술이 땡겼다.
examples.trans: I should have told everyone to go straight home, except I was craving a drink too.
This expression comes from 'was craving'.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: 방송 (broadcasting) + 국 (bureau/station)

examples.trans: I have to go to the TV station this afternoon.
Fans are waiting in front of the broadcasting station.

meanings.note: Korean says 시험을 보다 ('see an exam') for taking a test.

examples.trans: I am taking a Korean exam tomorrow.
Did you prepare well for the exam?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
Please come into the room.

examples.text: 올해 우리 회사에 신입사원이 많이 들어왔어요.
examples.trans: Many new employees joined our company this year.

meanings.note: Compound of 들다 (enter) + 오다 (come)

meanings.en: to join (a company, school, or group)

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 방송국에 시험 봐서 들어온 애가 경북 고령인지 경남 고령인지 구분이 안 되니?
examples.trans: You passed the entrance exam into a broadcasting station and cannot tell North Gyeongsang Goryeong from South Gyeongsang?
Here the word for 'distinction' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Describes something unusual or out of the ordinary.
Used when sensing something is wrong.

examples.trans: The computer sounds a bit strange.
It's suspicious that he's suddenly being so nice.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 경북 고령 이상하지 않니? 경남 고령이 자연스럽지!
examples.trans: Wait—does North Gyeongsang Goryeong not sound weird? South Gyeongsang Goryeong sounds natural!
This expression comes from 'sounds natural!'.

meanings.note: noun director

examples.trans: Director-nim.
Director's office.

meanings.note: Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 이렇다.
Used to emphasize degree.

examples.trans: You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 이게 이렇게 헷갈리는구나, 그럴수록 네가 더 신경을 썼어야지!
examples.trans: Oh, it really is confusing—which means you should have paid all the more attention!
This expression comes from 'really is confusing'.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

examples.text: 너 되게 정의롭다. 근데 신경 안 써도 돼.
examples.trans: You have quite a sense of justice. But you do not need to worry.

examples.text: 이 신발은 너무 신경 쓴 것 같잖아, 털털한 이미지인데.
examples.trans: These shoes look like I tried too hard when I am going for an easygoing image.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 고령 군청에 사과 전화 다 했고요, 다음 주에 사과 자막 넣기로 했어요.
examples.trans: We already phoned the county office to apologize and agreed to air an apology caption next week.
Here the word for 'to the county office' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 고령 군청에 사과 전화 다 했고요, 다음 주에 사과 자막 넣기로 했어요.
examples.trans: We already phoned the county office to apologize and agreed to air an apology caption next week.
Here the word for 'apology' is key.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.
I will hang up the phone.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used in 이번 주 (this week), 다음 주 (next week)

examples.trans: One week is seven days.
I'm going to go on a trip next week.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 자막은 신디가 손수 친 첫 야외 취침 텐트, 핑크로 해주시면 되고요.
examples.trans: For the caption, you can make it "Cindy's first hand-pitched outdoor tent" in pink.
Here the word for 'as for the caption' is key.
I want to put in right now.
How about trying to put in together tomorrow?
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.
Did you hear about this problem?
I was busy today because of problem.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.
Did you hear about this by our president?
I was busy today because of by our president.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 너 지금 그게 문제가 아니야, 우리 사장님 고향이 고령이야!
examples.trans: That is not the real problem right now—Goryeong is our station president's hometown!
Here the word for 'hometown' is key.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral, used for decimals, dates, money, etc.

examples.trans: The ratings came out at five percent.
Please wait just five minutes.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.trans: Oh my goodness!
Here the word for 'my' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.trans: Oh my goodness!
Here the word for 'gosh!' is key.
Did you hear about this chief, responsible?
I was busy today because of chief, responsible.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 이거 책임 소재 확실히 찾아, 그래야 나도 올라가서 보고할 때 할 말이 있지!
examples.trans: Pinpoint exactly who is responsible so I have something to say when I report upstairs!
Here the word for 'locus, where it lies' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 이거 책임 소재 확실히 찾아, 그래야 나도 올라가서 보고할 때 할 말이 있지!
examples.trans: Pinpoint exactly who is responsible so I have something to say when I report upstairs!
Here the word for 'clearly, definitely' is key.

meanings.note: Primary everyday meaning.
Used at a bank or ATM for taking out cash.

examples.trans: I withdrew money at the bank.
I am looking for my keys.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 가위바위보에서 졌다고 신디가 짐도 다 들고 올라갔대요.
examples.trans: Because she lost rock-paper-scissors, they say Cindy carried all the bags up herself.
This expression comes from 'they say she went up'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 이거 책임 소재 확실히 찾아, 그래야 나도 올라가서 보고할 때 할 말이 있지!
examples.trans: Pinpoint exactly who is responsible so I have something to say when I report upstairs!
This expression comes from 'when reporting'.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
